headline_findings.quote_safe: The average small service business lost 6.3% of booked appointments to no-shows (among 4,180 small service businesses using Example Booking Software, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026). That is far below the 18% to 30% figures still quoted from 2019 and 2020.
Businesses that sent both SMS and email reminders had an average no-show rate of 4.9%, against 10.0% for those that sent none (among 4,180 small service businesses using Example Booking Software).
Businesses that took a deposit averaged 3.8% no-shows, against 7.0% for those that didn't (among 4,180 small service businesses using Example Booking Software).
Fitness studios had the highest average no-show rate of the four industries, at 7.8%, against 5.7% for salons (among 4,180 small service businesses using Example Booking Software).
About 47% of owners said no-shows and late cancellations cost them more than 5% of revenue in the last 12 months (among 612 owners who answered).
About 38% of owners who take no deposit today plan to start taking one in the next 12 months (455 owners who answered).

report_outline: Title: The 2026 No-Show Report: what 4,180 small service businesses tell us about missed appointments
Key findings (one page): the headline findings in quote-safe wording, each with its base
1. How often clients miss appointments (F1, F4)
2. What goes with fewer misses: reminders and deposits (F2, F3)
3. What owners say no-shows cost them and why clients miss (F5, F6, F7, F8)
What we could not say (F9, F10 and the held-back group)
About the data and how to cite it
methods_section: What we measured. The share of booked appointments marked as a no-show, for each business, from 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. A business counts once, whatever its size: we computed each account's own rate and averaged the accounts, so a few very large accounts can't set the result. The pooled rate (all no-shows over all bookings) was 6.4%.

Who is in it. 4,180 businesses using Example Booking Software with at least 150 bookings in the period (5,938,687 bookings in all): 1,150 clinics, 1,080 fitness studios, 230 other businesses, 1,720 salons. These are our customers, not every small business, so every figure describes businesses like them.

The survey. 655 owners answered between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-29, recruited through an invitation in the company's monthly newsletter (customers and non-customers) and two posts in its own social channels. We removed 43 answers (29 incomplete, 6 duplicates, 8 completed in under a third of the median time), leaving 612; 251 of them are customers. Answers are not weighted.

Precision. Every figure has a 95% range. Survey shares use the normal interval, or the Wilson interval when a group has fewer than 30 answers or a share is under 10% or over 90%. Account averages use 1.96 standard errors across accounts. A survey figure leads the report only when its margin is 5 points or less (about 385 answers), and is shown at all only when it is 10 points or less (about 97 answers); account averages need a range within 10% of the value to lead and 20% to be shown.

Comparisons. We planned 5 comparisons before looking at the results and tested each at 0.05 / 5 = 0.01 (Bonferroni): Welch z-tests for account averages, two-proportion z-tests for survey shares. Differences are associations, not causes: businesses that take deposits or send reminders may differ in other ways.

Privacy. No figure comes from fewer than 10 businesses, and no business holds more than 30% of the bookings in any group shown. One group (other businesses that take a deposit) was too small to publish, so it and the group that would reveal it by subtraction are left out. We publish no customer names, and the data never left our warehouse in row form.
Conflict of interest. Example Booking Software sells booking software with reminders and deposits, the features this report compares.

stat_sheet.press_angle: The no-show figures quoted most often online come from 2019 and 2020 and run from 18% to 30%. Measured across 4,180 businesses, the average was 6.3%, and the gap between businesses with and without reminders or deposits is where the story is.
social_posts: Small service businesses lost 6.3% of bookings to no-shows in the 12 months to September 2026, not the 30% you keep reading. Data from 4,180 businesses in the 2026 No-Show Report.
No reminders: 10.0% no-shows. SMS and email reminders: 4.9%. Same year, 2,261 vs 643 businesses. More in the 2026 No-Show Report.
About 47% of owners say no-shows cost them more than 5% of revenue. About 38% of those without a deposit plan to add one. Survey of 612 owners.
stat_sheet.sales_line: Across 4,180 businesses on our platform, the ones sending SMS and email reminders averaged 4.9% no-shows against 10.0% for the ones sending none. That is an association across businesses, not a promise for yours, so we show the full method in the report.
